---
title: "Prop 40, the comparison: why the two estimates differ"
subtitle: "Teaching deck: the BSZ analysis (Boll, Saez and Zucman, August 2026) and the JR analysis (Jaros and Rauh, NBER, September 2026) on one common output"
output:
  xaringan::moon_reader:
    self_contained: true
    includes:
      in_header: mathjax-config.html
    css: [default, ../../../assets/paper.css, ../../../assets/paper-slides.css]
    nature:

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, fig.align = "center",
  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 150,
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE
)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 15))

# Every number in this deck is read from the files comparison/run.R writes
# (comparison/export/r/*.csv, through read_exports() in comparison/R/site.R) or recomputed
# from the two analyses' export contracts (read_contracts(), bridge_inputs()). Nothing is
# retyped except the authors' printed values, which come from the same files.
for (f in list.files("../../R", pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
root <- comparison_root()
ex <- read_exports(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r"))
k  <- read_contracts(root)
bi <- bridge_inputs(k); sup <- bi$sup; rj <- bi$rauh
vs <- score_common(sup); vr <- score_common(rj)          # the two ends, every term
ep <- ex$endpoints; en <- ex$ends; br <- ex$bridge; inp <- ex$inputs; hz <- ex$hoopes
own <- en[en$horizon_setting == "own", ]
ea <- own[own$output == "a", ]; eb <- own[own$output == "b", ]
epv <- function(id, col = "value") ep[[col]][ep$endpoint_id == id]
mv  <- function(key) ex$meta$value[ex$meta$key == key]
rj_main  <- epv("rauh_nber_npv", "contract_value")       # the JR main estimate (seeded run)
rj_print <- epv("rauh_nber_npv", "printed_value")
bsz_print <- epv("bsz_tab5_row1", "printed_value")
oi <- k$rjkdc$inputs
ceiling72 <- pick(oi, "nber_ceiling_hardcoded")
f_lo <- pick(oi, "nber_mc_f_min"); f_hi <- pick(oi, "nber_mc_f_max")

# Money in prose. A literal dollar sign is safe here because the deck uses no inline math.
# Wrapped so a line never breaks between the minus sign and the amount.
usd <- function(x, d = 1, signed = FALSE) paste0('<span class="nb">', money(x, d, signed), "</span>")
num <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")

# The bridge on output (b) at each analysis's own horizon, and on (a).
bb <- br[br$horizon_setting == "own" & br$output == "b", ]
ba <- br[br$horizon_setting == "own" & br$output == "a", ]
sh  <- function(id, b = bb) b$shapley[b$step_id == id]
sq  <- function(id, b = bb) b$sequential[b$step_id == id]
bb_sorted <- bb[order(-abs(bb$shapley)), ]
top3 <- bb_sorted[1:3, ]; rest <- bb_sorted[-(1:3), ]
gap_b <- eb$bsz_model - eb$rauh_own
steps <- bridge_steps()
# The dial path (R/model.R dial_path()): the explorer's dials moved top to bottom, each to its
# far end. The pseudo-equation reads it, as the explorer and the overview do.
dp <- read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r", "dial_path.csv"))

# Ties to the pipeline: a drift fails the render instead of shipping.
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(vs[["a"]], ea$bsz_model)), isTRUE(all.equal(vs[["b"]], eb$bsz_model)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(vr[["a"]], ea$rauh_own)),  isTRUE(all.equal(vr[["b"]], eb$rauh_own)),
  abs(sum(bb$shapley) + gap_b) < 1e-9,
  abs(sum(bb$sequential) + gap_b) < 1e-9,
  abs(sum(dp$change) + gap_b) < 1e-9, identical(dp$step_id, EXPLORER_DIAL_ORDER),
  # the deck names these three as the main differences, in this order
  identical(top3$step_id, c("litigation_survival", "horizon", "income_loss_share")),
  round(rj_main, 1) == rj_print,
  isTRUE(all.equal(mv("A_5"), expected_annuity(5, sup$r_min, sup$r_max))))

# The BSZ overview discounts at one rate, the middle of the range; the two agree to $0.01B.
r_mid <- (sup$r_min + sup$r_max) / 2
bsz_mid <- vs[["a"]] + vs[["X"]] - vs[["annual_loss"]] * (1 - (1 + r_mid)^(-sup$H)) / r_mid
stopifnot(abs(bsz_mid - eb$bsz_model) < 0.01)

# R against the Python twin (comparison/export/py/), as in the report's "What reproduces".
pdir <- file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "py")
py_ok <- dir.exists(pdir)
maxdiff <- if (py_ok) max(vapply(c("ends", "bridge", "endpoints"), function(f) {
  r <- read_csv_plain(file.path(root, "comparison", "export", "r", paste0(f, ".csv")))
  p <- read_csv_plain(file.path(pdir, paste0(f, ".csv")))
  key <- intersect(c("horizon_setting", "output", "step_id", "endpoint_id"), names(r))
  p <- p[match(do.call(paste, r[key]), do.call(paste, p[key])), ]
  cols <- setdiff(names(r)[vapply(r, is.numeric, TRUE)], "sequential_rank")
  max(vapply(cols, function(cc) max(abs(r[[cc]] - as.numeric(p[[cc]])), na.rm = TRUE), 0))
}, 0)) else NA
```

# An Open Comparison

.opa-intro[
Two analyses of California's Billionaire Tax Act reach opposite signs. This deck puts both on
one common output and walks from one to the other, one disputed input at a time, following the
[Open Policy Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1093/scipol/scaa067) framework.
]

and [the materials page](../materials.html), the code, its tests and every exported CSV
]

---
name: estimates

# Two analyses, two main estimates

.pull-left[

**The BSZ analysis** (Boll, Saez and Zucman, NBER Working Paper 35218, August 2026)

.big[`r usd(eb$bsz_model)`]

Net total over 5 years, in today's dollars. It is the wealth tax collected
(`r usd(ea$bsz_model)`; the paper prints `r usd(bsz_print, 0)`, Table 5 row 1), plus the income tax
from assets sold to pay it, minus the income tax lost to those who leave.<sup>1</sup>

]

.pull-right[

**The JR analysis** (Jaros and Rauh, NBER chapter c15504, September 2026)

.big[`r usd(rj_main)`]

Mean net present value. It is the wealth tax minus the income tax lost for ever, averaged over
the authors' Monte Carlo (a simulation that draws the uncertain inputs at random many times
and averages the results).

]

.blue-box[
**Net present value**: all gains minus all losses, with each future dollar converted to its
value today (discounted). One analysis says the state
gains about `r usd(eb$bsz_model, 0)`. The other says it loses about `r usd(-rj_main, 0)`.
]

.footnote[<sup>1</sup> BSZ's own headline is the wealth tax alone. The net total is this OPA's choice, so both main estimates answer the same question. The BSZ overview discounts at `r pct(r_mid, 0)`; this deck averages over a rate range ([the common output](#common-output)); both give `r usd(eb$bsz_model)`.]

---
name: common-output

# Why the printed numbers are not comparable

The BSZ paper asks **how much the tax collects**. The JR paper asks **whether the state is
better off**, once income tax lost to departures is subtracted. So the comparison defines two
common outputs and estimates both analyses on each:

.highlight-box[
**(a) gross revenue** = the one-time wealth tax collected<br>
**(b) net fiscal effect** = (a) + extra income tax from assets sold to pay the tax
&minus; income tax lost to departures, counted for H years and discounted
]

```{r tab-outputs, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Analysis</th><th>(a) gross revenue</th><th>(b) net fiscal effect</th><th>What the authors print</th></tr>')
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>BSZ analysis</td><td>%s</td><td><b>%s</b></td><td>%s revenue (Table 5 row 1); no net figure</td></tr>',
            usd(ea$bsz_model), usd(eb$bsz_model), usd(bsz_print, 0)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>JR analysis</td><td>%s</td><td><b>%s</b></td><td>mean NPV %s; revenue "approximately %s"</td></tr>',
            usd(ea$rauh_own), usd(eb$rauh_own), usd(rj_print), usd(pick(k$docs, "nber_headline_revenue"), 0)))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
The horizon H is itself disputed: 5 years for the BSZ analysis, for ever for the JR analysis.
Discounting uses the JR analysis's rate, drawn between `r pct(sup$r_min, 1)` and
`r pct(sup$r_max, 1)`; the BSZ analysis takes no position on the rate. Output (b) is the one both
main estimates answer, so the rest of the deck uses it. For the JR analysis both outputs are exact
averages of the authors' Monte Carlo, so (b) is `r usd(eb$rauh_own)` against the `r usd(rj_print)`
of their one seeded run.
]

---
name: term-wealth

# One function, term 1: the wealth tax collected

.highlight-box[
**Wealth tax collected** = 5% &times; the base &times; (1 &minus; share already departed)
&times; (1 &minus; avoidance allowance) &times; chance the tax survives litigation
]

```{r tab-wealth, results="asis"}
w_s <- sup$W_core + sup$W_noncit; w_r <- rj$W_core + rj$W_noncit
dshare <- function(x) score_common(x)[["d_conf"]]
run_s <- cumprod(c(w_s, sup$tau, 1 - sup$re, 1 - dshare(sup), 1 - sup$alpha, sup$q))
run_r <- cumprod(c(w_r, rj$tau, 1 - rj$re, 1 - dshare(rj), 1 - rj$alpha, rj$q))
stopifnot(abs(run_s[6] - vs[["a"]]) < 1e-9, abs(run_r[6] - vr[["a"]]) < 1e-9)
fac <- function(x) pct(x, if (abs(100 * x - round(100 * x)) < 1e-9) 0 else 1)
rows <- list(
  c("Wealth on the list", usd(w_s, 0), usd(w_s, 0), usd(w_r, 0), usd(w_r, 0)),
  c("&times; tax rate", fac(sup$tau), usd(run_s[2]), fac(rj$tau), usd(run_r[2])),
  c("&times; (1 &minus; real-estate deduction)", fac(1 - sup$re), usd(run_s[3]), fac(1 - rj$re), usd(run_r[3])),
  c("&times; (1 &minus; share already departed)", fac(1 - dshare(sup)), usd(run_s[4]), fac(1 - dshare(rj)), usd(run_r[4])),
  c("&times; (1 &minus; avoidance allowance)", fac(1 - sup$alpha), usd(run_s[5]), fac(1 - rj$alpha), usd(run_r[5])),
  c("&times; chance it survives litigation, <i>q</i>", fac(sup$q), usd(run_s[6]), fac(rj$q), usd(run_r[6])))
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Step</th><th>BSZ factor</th><th>BSZ running total</th><th>JR factor</th><th>JR running total</th></tr>')
for (r in rows) cat("<tr><td>", paste(r, collapse = "</td><td>"), "</td></tr>")
cat(sprintf('<tr class="tot"><td>= (a) wealth tax collected</td><td></td><td>%s</td><td></td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["a"]]), usd(vr[["a"]])))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
The BSZ base is California's billionaires on 1 July 2026, non-US citizens included. The JR base
is the 2025 Forbes list grown `r pct(pick(oi, "nber_growth_rate"))` to 31 December 2026, net of
real estate, after seven confirmed departures. The **litigation weight *q*** is the chance the Act
survives a court challenge; the revenue is multiplied by it.
]

---
name: term-loss

# One function, term 2: the income tax lost

.highlight-box[
**Income tax lost** = share lost &times; yearly income tax &times; years counted, discounted
]

```{r tab-loss, results="asis"}
stopifnot(abs(vs[["annual_loss"]] * vs[["annuity"]] - vs[["PV"]]) < 1e-9,
          abs(vr[["annual_loss"]] * vr[["annuity"]] - vr[["PV"]]) < 1e-9)
hz_txt <- function(H) if (is.infinite(H)) "for ever" else paste(H, "years")
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Step</th><th>BSZ analysis</th><th>JR analysis</th></tr>')
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>Share of billionaire income tax lost</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', pct(vs[["f"]], 0), pct(vr[["f"]], 0)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>&times; billionaires&#39; yearly California income tax</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(sup$C, 2), usd(rj$C, 2)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>= yearly loss</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["annual_loss"]], 2), usd(vr[["annual_loss"]], 2)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>&times; value today of 1 dollar a year, %s for BSZ, %s for JR</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
            hz_txt(sup$H), hz_txt(rj$H), num(vs[["annuity"]]), num(vr[["annuity"]])))
cat(sprintf('<tr class="tot"><td>= income tax lost, in today&#39;s dollars</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["PV"]], 2), usd(vr[["PV"]], 2)))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
- **Share lost**: the share of billionaires' yearly California income tax that leaves with
  those who move. BSZ: `r pct(sup$m, 0)` of their `r pct(sup$alpha, 0)` avoidance allowance is people moving,
  so `r pct(vs[["f"]], 0)` of the income tax leaves. JR: a flat `r pct(rj$f0, 0)`, the middle of a random draw between
  `r pct(f_lo, 0)` and `r pct(f_hi, 0)`.
- **Value today of 1 dollar a year**: a dollar a year for 5 years is worth `r num(mv("A_5"))` dollars
  today. A **perpetuity**, a dollar every year for ever, is worth 1/r at rate r: `r num(mv("A_inf"))`
  dollars, averaged over the `r pct(sup$r_min, 1)` to `r pct(sup$r_max, 1)` rates.
]

---
name: two-ends

# The two ends on output (b)

.highlight-box[
**Net fiscal effect (b)** = wealth tax collected + income tax from assets sold to pay
&minus; income tax lost
]

```{r tab-ends, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th></th><th>BSZ analysis</th><th>JR analysis</th></tr>')
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>Wealth tax collected, (a)</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["a"]], 2), usd(vr[["a"]], 2)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>+ income tax from assets sold to pay the tax</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["X"]], 2), usd(vr[["X"]], 2)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>&minus; income tax lost, in today&#39;s dollars</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["PV"]], 2), usd(vr[["PV"]], 2)))
cat(sprintf('<tr class="tot"><td>= (b) net fiscal effect</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(vs[["b"]], 2), usd(vr[["b"]], 2)))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
- **Assets sold to pay.** BSZ assume `r fmt_input("s", sup$s)` of the tax is paid by selling
  assets, `r pct(sup$g, 0)` of each sale is a taxable gain, and California taxes gains at
  `r pct(sup$t_cg, 1)`. The JR analysis does not model it.
- **The JR end** is `r usd(eb$rauh_own, 2)`, the exact average of the authors' Monte Carlo,
  computed by formula. The authors print `r usd(rj_print)` from one run of the random draws
  started from a fixed seed, which the JR reproduction gives as `r usd(rj_main, 2)`.
]

.blue-box[
The same function returns both ends exactly. The gap to explain is
`r usd(eb$bsz_model, 2)` &minus; (`r usd(eb$rauh_own, 2)`) = **`r usd(gap_b, 2)`**.
]

---
name: shapley-toy

# The bridge: switch one input at a time

```{r toy}
# A toy, not the real inputs: revenue = base x (1 - departed) x q, with two inputs to switch.
toy_base <- 100; d_from <- 0; d_to <- 0.3; q_from <- 1; q_to <- 0.5
toy <- function(d, q) toy_base * (1 - d) * q
t_start <- toy(d_from, q_from); t_end <- toy(d_to, q_to)
o1_d <- toy(d_to, q_from) - t_start; o1_q <- t_end - toy(d_to, q_from)   # departures first
o2_q <- toy(d_from, q_to) - t_start; o2_d <- t_end - toy(d_from, q_to)   # litigation first
phi_d <- (o1_d + o2_d) / 2; phi_q <- (o1_q + o2_q) / 2
stopifnot(abs(phi_d + phi_q - (t_end - t_start)) < 1e-12)
tm <- function(x) paste0(if (x < 0) "&minus;" else "", "$", formatC(abs(x), format = "f", digits = 1), "B")
```

A toy. Revenue = `r tm(toy_base)` &times; (1 &minus; share departed) &times; *q*. One analysis has
nobody departed and *q* = `r q_from`: `r tm(t_start)`. The other has `r pct(d_to)` departed and
*q* = `r q_to`: `r tm(t_end)`. The gap is `r tm(t_end - t_start)`. How much of it is each input?

```{r toy-tab, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Order of the switches</th><th>Departures step</th><th>Litigation step</th><th>Sum</th></tr>')
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>Departures first, then litigation</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', tm(o1_d), tm(o1_q), tm(o1_d + o1_q)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>Litigation first, then departures</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', tm(o2_d), tm(o2_q), tm(o2_d + o2_q)))
cat(sprintf('<tr class="tot"><td>Average over the two orders</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', tm(phi_d), tm(phi_q), tm(phi_d + phi_q)))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
The inputs multiply, so each step's size depends on what was switched before it. Litigation
halves `r tm(toy_base)` if it goes first, but only `r tm(toy(d_to, q_from))` if it goes second.
]

.blue-box[
The **Shapley value** of an input is its step averaged over every order of the switches. The
averages always add up to the whole gap. The real bridge has `r nrow(steps)` inputs, so
`r format(factorial(nrow(steps)), big.mark = ",")` orders; the code computes the average exactly
by running the function at all `r format(2^nrow(steps), big.mark = ",")` mixes of BSZ and JR values.
]

---
name: waterfall

# The bridge on output (b): `r sum(abs(bb$shapley) > 1e-12)` Shapley steps

```{r waterfall, fig.height=3.75}
B <- build_series(ex)$own$b$shapley
run <- 0; rows <- list()
for (i in seq_along(B)) {
  b <- B[[i]]
  if (b$type == "total") { y0 <- 0; y1 <- b$value; run <- b$value } else { y0 <- run; y1 <- run + b$value; run <- y1 }
  rows[[i]] <- data.frame(i = i, short = b$short, y0 = y0, y1 = y1, v = b$value, type = b$type,
                          fill = if (b$type == "total") "an analysis's estimate" else if (b$type == "model") "model difference"
                                 else if (b$value >= 0) "step that raises it" else "step that lowers it")
}
wf <- do.call(rbind, rows)
stopifnot(abs(wf$y1[nrow(wf) - 1] - eb$rauh_own) < 1e-9)
wf$lab <- ifelse(wf$type == "total", vapply(wf$v, money, "", digits = 1),
                 vapply(wf$v, money, "", digits = 1, signed = TRUE))
wf$ly <- ifelse(wf$type == "total", ifelse(wf$v >= 0, wf$y1, wf$y1), pmin(wf$y0, wf$y1))
wf$vj <- ifelse(wf$type == "total" & wf$v >= 0, -0.4, 1.4)
ggplot(wf) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#5b6873", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = i - 0.38, xmax = i + 0.38, ymin = pmin(y0, y1), ymax = pmax(y0, y1), fill = fill)) +
  geom_text(aes(x = i, y = ly, label = lab, vjust = vj), size = 3.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("an analysis's estimate" = "#222222", "model difference" = "#c8c8c8",
                               "step that raises it" = "#555555", "step that lowers it" = "#9a9a9a"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = wf$i, labels = wf$short) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "$ billion") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1), legend.position = "top",
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), plot.margin = margin(2, 4, 0, 4))
```

.small[
Each bar switches one input from the BSZ value to the JR value, at its Shapley value. Every step
but one lowers the estimate. Dropping the BSZ `r pct(sup$alpha, 0)` avoidance allowance raises it, because the
JR analysis applies none.
]

---
name: pseudo-eq

# What separates the two numbers

```{r pseudo, results="asis"}
# the eight terms of the dial path, in the explorer's order, each with its symbol and the
# running value (the same equation as the explorer and the overview)
path_label <- function(i) if (dp$step_id[i] == "minor_inputs") dp$title[i] else paste0(dp$title[i], " (", dp$symbol[i], ")")
term <- function(i) sprintf('<span class="eq-step"><span class="op">%s</span><span class="term"><b>%s</b><small>%s</small><span class="run">to %s</span></span></span>',
                            if (dp$change[i] < 0) "&minus;" else "+", money(abs(dp$change[i]), 1),
                            esc(path_label(i)), money(dp$to[i], 1))
cat('<div class="pseudo-eq">',
    sprintf('<span class="term"><b>%s</b><small>BSZ estimate</small></span>', money(eb$bsz_model, 1)),
    paste(vapply(seq_len(nrow(dp)), term, ""), collapse = ""),
    sprintf('<span class="eq-step"><span class="op">&asymp;</span><span class="term"><b>%s</b><small>JR estimate</small></span></span>', money(eb$rauh_own, 1)),
    '</div>', sep = "")
```

.small[
Move the BSZ panel's dials top to bottom, each to its far end: each term is what that dial
changes. The terms add up exactly; "about equal" is only rounding. The JR estimate here is the
exact average, `r usd(eb$rauh_own, 2)`. The printed seeded run is `r usd(rj_print)`.
]

The next three slides take the three inputs with the largest Shapley values, which do not
depend on an order. Each says what both analyses assume, why, and what kind of claim it is:

.small[
- **data**: settled by observable facts (lists, filings, tax statistics)
- **research**: a parameter taken from published studies
- **guesswork**: asserted without data or a study behind it, legal judgements included
- **scenario**: a choice of which world to estimate, which neither data nor studies settle
]

---
name: diff-litigation

# Difference 1: will the tax survive in court?

```{r claims-fn}
claim_table <- function(bsz, jr) {
  cat('<table class="dt claims"><tr><th style="width:50%">The BSZ analysis</th><th>The JR analysis</th></tr>')
  cat(sprintf("<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>", bsz, jr))
  cat("</table>")
}
```

```{r claims-lit, results="asis"}
claim_table(
  sprintf("<b><i>q</i> = %s.</b> The Act as written, collected in full. Neither BSZ nor the expert report it builds on (GGSS: Galle, Gamage, Saez and Shanske) discounts the revenue for litigation risk (BSZ Table 5; GGSS p.4).", fmt_input("q", sup$q)),
  sprintf("<b><i>q</i> = %s.</b> The chance the Act survives a court challenge, set at the &quot;more likely than not&quot; threshold of an accounting rule (ASC 740-10; NBER README, chapter Sec. 4.3). The Monte Carlo draws the revenue anywhere between zero (struck down) and the %s ceiling; its average is half the ceiling.", fmt_input("q", rj$q), usd(ceiling72, 0)))
```

.pull-left[

**Kind of claim:** <span class="og guesswork">guesswork</span>, a legal judgement. No data or study
gives the chance a court upholds this Act.

**Why it is large:** *q* multiplies the whole revenue, so halving it halves what the other inputs
leave.

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
**Dollars moved, on (b):** `r usd(sh("litigation_survival"), 1, TRUE)` (Shapley), the largest step.
On (a), the revenue alone: `r usd(sh("litigation_survival", ba), 1, TRUE)`.
]

.small[The lost income tax is not scaled by *q*: people who left do not come back if the Act is struck down.]

]

---
name: diff-horizon

# Difference 2: for how long is the income tax lost?

```{r claims-hz, results="asis"}
claim_table(
  sprintf("<b>%s.</b> The losses are &quot;annual temporary&quot; and last about the five payment years (&quot;If they last say only 5 years&quot;, BSZ PDF p.27). A one-time tax should cause a temporary response (BSZ p.22).", fmt_input("H", sup$H)),
  sprintf("<b>%s.</b> A billionaire who leaves stops paying California income tax for ever, so the lost stream is valued as a perpetuity, 1/r (chapter Sec. 5.4, eq. 18-19).", tools::toTitleCase(fmt_input("H", rj$H))))
```

```{r tab-hz, results="asis"}
ls <- ex$loss; l_b <- ls[ls$source_id == "bsz_row1", ]; l_r <- ls[ls$source_id == "rauh_nber", ]
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Income tax lost, in today&#39;s dollars</th><th>5 years</th><th>For ever</th><th>Moving to for ever</th></tr>')
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>BSZ yearly loss, %s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(l_b$annual_loss, 2), usd(l_b$pv_5yr), usd(l_b$pv_perpetuity), usd(l_b$pv_5yr - l_b$pv_perpetuity, 1, TRUE)))
cat(sprintf('<tr><td>JR yearly loss, %s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', usd(l_r$annual_loss, 2), usd(l_r$pv_5yr), usd(l_r$pv_perpetuity), usd(l_r$pv_5yr - l_r$pv_perpetuity, 1, TRUE)))
cat("</table>")
```

.pull-left[

**Kind of claim:** <span class="og scenario">scenario</span>. Neither data nor studies settle how
long a departure lasts.

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
**Dollars moved, on (b):** `r usd(sh("horizon"), 1, TRUE)` (Shapley). The perpetuity multiplies
whatever yearly loss the other inputs imply. So the step lies between the two rows of the table.
]

]

---
name: diff-share

# Difference 3: how much of the income tax leaves?

```{r claims-sh, results="asis"}
claim_table(
  sprintf("<b>The loss follows the people who leave.</b> What is lost is the leavers' own income tax, from SEC filings for the largest fortunes and a wealth-proportional rate for the rest (BSZ PDF p.26, Table 4): %s a year in its aggressive scenario. With no departures at the BSZ end, only the movers count: %s of the %s allowance, so %s.",
          usd(bi$ladder$L[2], 2), pct(sup$m), pct(sup$alpha), pct(vs[["f"]])),
  sprintf("<b>A flat %s.</b> The middle of a random draw between %s and %s, independent of how much revenue is collected (NPV_dist_v8.R; chapter Sec. 5.4). It does not depend on who leaves.",
          pct(rj$f0), pct(f_lo), pct(f_hi)))
```

.pull-left[

**Kind of claim:** <span class="og data">data</span> against <span class="og guesswork">guesswork</span>.
The BSZ ratio rests on tax filings. The JR range is asserted.

**Share lost** is the share of billionaires' yearly California income tax that leaves the state
with those who move.

]

.pull-right[

.highlight-box[
**Dollars moved, on (b):** `r usd(sh("income_loss_share"), 1, TRUE)` (Shapley).
]

.small[In one fixed order (the order of [Hoopes 2026](#hoopes)) this step comes before the horizon,
while the loss still lasts 5 years, and moves only `r usd(sq("income_loss_share"), 1, TRUE)`.]

]

name: smaller

# The smaller steps

```{r tab-rest, results="asis"}
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Input</th><th>BSZ value</th><th>JR value</th><th class="l">Kind of claim</th><th>Shapley on (b)</th></tr>')
for (i in seq_len(nrow(rest))) {
  tx <- step_texts(inp, rest$step_id[i])
  cat(sprintf('<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td class="l">%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
              esc(rest$title[i]), tx$bsz, tx$rjkdc, rest$kind[i], money(rest$shapley[i], 1, TRUE)))
}
cat(sprintf('<tr class="tot"><td>The %d together</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td>%s</td></tr>', nrow(rest), money(sum(rest$shapley), 1, TRUE)))
cat("</table>")
```

.small[
- **Billionaires already departed** is close to the three above. The JR analysis removes seven
  confirmed departures, `r pct(dshare(rj), 1)` of its base; the BSZ analysis taxes everyone resident
  on 1 January 2026. "Guesswork on data" means a legal judgement about residency applied to who
  announced a move.
- **Yearly income tax**: BSZ take the 2019 to 2025 average from tax statistics and published
  research. JR take the middle of a range whose floor is the authors' judgement.
- **Avoidance and evasion allowance** is the one step that raises the estimate. The JR analysis
  applies no allowance beyond departures, so dropping the BSZ `r pct(sup$alpha, 0)` adds revenue.
]

---
name: hoopes

# The one published comparison: Hoopes (2026)

.small[
Jeffrey Hoopes, "Galle v Rauh" (SSRN 6428578), compares **earlier versions**: the February 2026
GGSS expert report, on which the BSZ analysis builds, and the March 2026 version by Rauh, Jaros,
Kearney, Doran and Cosso. His Figure 2 is a waterfall that prints no values, so his column is read
off the chart. Ours follows his order and ends at the September 2026 version.
]

```{r tab-hoopes, results="asis"}
lab <- k$hoopes$step_label[match(hz$step_id, k$hoopes$step_id)]
keep <- !is.na(lab) | abs(hz$ours) > 1e-9
lab[is.na(lab)] <- paste0("(no bar: ", hz$our_steps[is.na(lab)], ")")
hm <- function(x, first) if (is.na(x)) "none" else money(x, 1, !first)
cat('<table class="dt"><tr><th>Hoopes Figure 2 bar</th><th>Hoopes (read off the chart)</th><th>Ours, his order</th></tr>')
for (i in which(keep)) {
  first <- hz$step_id[i] == "galle_estimate"
  cat(sprintf('<tr><td>%s</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>', esc(lab[i]), hm(hz$hoopes[i], first), hm(hz$ours[i], first)))
}
cat(sprintf('<tr class="tot"><td>Where the waterfall ends</td><td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
            money(sum(hz$hoopes, na.rm = TRUE), 1), money(sum(hz$ours, na.rm = TRUE), 1)))
cat("</table>")
stopifnot(abs(sum(hz$ours, na.rm = TRUE) - eb$rauh_own) < 1e-9)
```

.small[
The residency bars agree. The income tax bars differ by `r usd(abs(hz$hoopes[hz$step_id == "income_tax_loss"] - hz$ours[hz$step_id == "income_tax_loss"]))`. The departures and behaviour bars differ because
the versions differ: September counts seven departures on a grown base and adds the litigation
weight; March used an elasticity response and ten "expanded" departures, which September does not.
]

name: next

# What reproduces, and where to go next

.pull-left[

**What reproduces**

.small[
- At the BSZ inputs the function returns Table 5 row 1, `r usd(ea$bsz_model, 3)` (printed `r usd(bsz_print, 0)`).
- At the JR inputs it returns the exact average of the authors' Monte Carlo, `r usd(eb$rauh_own, 3)`
  (printed `r usd(rj_print)` from one seeded run).
- The Shapley steps add up to the gap, and a test checks them against a brute-force average over orders.
- A Python twin writes the same tables. The largest difference from R is `r if (py_ok) formatC(maxdiff, format = "e", digits = 1) else "not checked"`; the tests require 1e-9.
- **Not reproduced here:** the comparison takes each analysis's exported inputs and outputs as
  given. Each analysis's own reproduction is on its overview page.
]

]

.pull-right[

**Where to go next**

.small[

- [The report](../repro.html): every step in a table, with the R and Python code in folds
- [The materials page](../materials.html) and [the repository](https://github.com/fhoces/opa-prop40/tree/main/comparison)
- [The comparison overview](../../../index.html)
- [The BSZ analysis](../../../bsz-analysis/site/) and [the JR analysis](../../../rjkdc-analysis/site/), each with its own deck
]

]

The bridge shows where the `r usd(gap_b, 0)` gap comes from. It cannot say which value of each input is right.
